preamble: Each claim states what it covers, what kind of evidence stands behind it, and what it does not show. Evidence classes: implementation (the code or document exists), automated (a test or probe in this repository), system (observed in a real system), human (a recorded observation), comparative (matched measurement against an alternative). A claim is `supported` only with automated or system evidence; it is marked verified only with system evidence at an exact revision. Automated evidence carries the commit at which its tests were last run green; any later change to its cited path makes it a candidate for re-running (`node scripts/claim-ledger.mjs --check --stale`). No claim in the first seeding has system-class evidence at a known revision, so none is marked verified. Publication, tag and visibility decisions are not made by this file.

claims.claim: The default model id is zai/glm-5.3, with precedence --model, then SHIP_MODEL, then config file, then default.
claims.scope: Model id resolution only (src/model-id.ts). Says nothing about how well that model performs.

evidence.test: flag wins over env and config
an empty SHIP_MODEL falls through to config, then the default

limitations: Resolution of the id string only; whether the configured gateway serves it is not checked.

claims.claim: glm-5.3 resolved 35 of 50 seeded SWE-bench Lite instances.
claims.scope: Seeded 50-of-300 Lite subset, official evaluator, bare configuration (not the product path), recorded 2026-08-16. Not a Ship product result and not a held-out result.
limitations: The writeup does not pin a Ship commit; the system evidence is therefore not counted.

Other models have little or no evidence: claude-haiku-4-5 was 1/9 on a hand-picked set with prompts tuned against GLM; claude-sonnet-5 3/3 and 6/6 on small saturated in-house suites; none for OpenAI-shaped, Gemini, DeepSeek, Opus or local models.
Not the product path, so it does not support any claim about Ship tasks.

claims.claim: Steering notes are offered and accepted only for runs whose harness can consume them, which is the native harness only.
claims.scope: The capability table in src/harness-capabilities.ts, as consulted by the run page and the steering route.

evidence.test: S13: only the native harness takes steering notes
S13: a multi-harness run supports a capability only if every attempt does

limitations: The table is tested; the route refusal itself has no automated test.
No live steering of a real native run is recorded.
External harnesses (claude-code, opencode) cannot be steered; that is a gap, not a feature.

claims.claim: External harnesses refuse plan review: a run that requires plan review fails with an explicit error and starts no external agent.
claims.scope: claude-code and opencode adapters, at admission (runtime) and on direct workflow execution.

evidence.test: direct external execution cannot bypass requested plan review

limitations: The test drives a fake claude binary; the admission-time check in src/runtime.ts has no dedicated cited test here.
No real external harness run was observed.

claims.claim: A delivery stuck in executing past the stale window is recognised as stale only by state and age, and stale rollback reconciliation reads the target before deciding.
claims.scope: src/delivery.ts state machine with in-memory and fake targets. Delivery execution is off without SHIP_DELIVERY_DIR.

evidence.test: isStaleExecuting keys on state and age, above the execution ceiling
gap: stale rollback reconciliation reads the target

limitations: No live forge or deployment target was exercised.
The stale window is a fixed 35 minutes by default.

claims.claim: Authenticated clone and warm fetch scrub the remote in the same shell invocation as the credential, whatever the credentialed step returns.
claims.scope: src/git.ts clone and warm-volume fetch through an executor.

evidence.test: S01: authenticated clone and fetch scrub the remote in the same shell invocation as the credential

limitations: The sequencing test fails on the previous code; the failed-fetch probe on a real checkout is a regression pin only (the old path also scrubbed).
Not proven through the Sandbox daemon or a live private repository.

claims.claim: SHIP_GIT_CREDENTIAL=env keeps the Git token out of every command line and out of .git/config.
claims.scope: LocalExecutor with a real git and a local HTTP server. Implemented, OFF by default (argv mode remains the default).

evidence.test: S01: env credential mode keeps the token out of argv and the URL, argv mode does not
S01: a real git clone in env mode sends the credential as a header and never puts it in argv or config

limitations: Unproven live: the Sandbox daemon must forward per-exec env, and the sandbox git must be 2.31 or later.
No private-repo clone or push on Forgejo or GitHub through the real sandbox has been run.
Default unchanged; see AUDIT_OPEN.md before flipping it.

claims.claim: The retained product-journey records count 15 pass, 5 fail, 6 unknown and 2 harness-error over 28 attempts in 20 runs.
claims.scope: evals/product-journeys/results at the recount of 2026-10-03, using the recorded outcome where present and outcomeOf otherwise. A development and regression set, not held-out, and not a model-quality number.

evidence.test: each outcome class is counted exactly once and unknown is neither pass nor fail
negative control: an unknown record is in no pass or fail count and no denominator

limitations: The counting rules are tested on synthetic trees; the figures themselves are the generated report, not a separate test.
Costs: 12 records priced, 16 unknown; the priced sum is a lower bound.
Supplements (one regrade, one reclassification) are listed but not applied.

claims.claim: The earlier headline of 21 passes, 13 failures and 2 human-gated harness errors over 36 attempts is not claimed.
claims.scope: It cannot be reproduced from the retained records; 8 of the 36 attempts are not in this repository. The private receipts it may come from were not available.
limitations: Do not quote 21/13/2. Use eval.retained-recount, with its scope.
Not shown to be wrong either: the missing records were not checked.

claims.claim: A tailnet preview container can reach the internet, the LAN, the tailnet and other containers on the shared bridge; it is not restricted by the sandbox allowlist.
claims.scope: Previews started by teploy preview deploy on the preview target. The defect is in the CLI, so the owning layer is teploy-cli.
limitations: No Ship-side change made; any isolation claim for previews is withheld until the CLI change and a live proof on the preview target exist.
A successful preview is not evidence that production isolation guarantees exist.

claims.claim: Command-regex approval classification is advisory, not an enforcement boundary.
claims.scope: defaultApprovalPolicy and sandboxApprovalPolicy classification of raw Bash and Python source, most relevant to the trusted-local executor. Open item teploy-ship-04.
limitations: Equivalent operations through other commands, APIs, indirection or argument forms may not be recognised.
Deferred as a design project: capability-scoped executor boundaries and a policy corpus of equivalent spellings are not built.
This is not evidence of an escape from the separate sandbox implementation.

claims.claim: No claim is made that Ship is better than, faster than or more capable than any other product.
claims.scope: The programme treats competitor material as documented design references, not measured quality.
limitations: A superiority claim needs matched direct comparative evidence on named dimensions; none exists.
